title: Learn How to Design Software Systems Like a Senior Engineer in Our New Course
summary: freeCodeCamp.org published a free 3-hour YouTube course teaching system design using a five-step framework for structuring thinking and tackling vague requirements under interview pressure. The course walks through building high-level architectures for real-world systems like Spotify, Booking.com, and WhatsApp, covering bottleneck identification, time management, storage and traffic estimation, and trade-off discussions such as WebSockets versus HTTP or when to add load balancers. It also explains the five dimensions candidates are evaluated on during system design interviews.

title: LittleJS is 2D and 3D now
summary: LittleJS, the small dependency-free HTML5 game engine, has shipped its biggest update yet: a full 3D renderer that shares the canvas with 2D rendering, letting objects from both mix freely with shared physics, children, and timers. New built-in 2D and 3D level editors, a one-line particle effects library, and reworked rendering (batched WebGL2 sprites, instanced 3D drawing) make it faster, verified against PixiJS, Three.js, PlayCanvas, Phaser, and Babylon.js in a new open WebGL Engine Bench. The engine also gains AI-focused tooling: a LittleJS AI toolkit with starter templates and agent instructions, a Claude Code plugin that scaffolds playable projects in two commands, a LittleJS GPT for no-code game building, and an arcade of 50+ open-source example games. A new site, littlejsengine.com, demos all the features, and a third community game jam is running October 2 to November 2.

title: Pele – Mermaid diagrams as themeable SVG
summary: Pele is a lightweight, zero-dependency open source library that renders Mermaid diagram syntax to SVG, themed entirely with CSS variables. Built for Obsidian, it claims a bundle size 6x smaller and render times up to 500x faster than Mermaid.js, while supporting every diagram type in Mermaid 12.1.0. Color changes apply without re-rendering, and the library adapts diagram layouts for small screens rather than just scaling them.

title: HTTP1 vs HTTP2 vs HTTP3
summary: A primer on foundational HTTP and networking concepts that explain why web pages feel slow even when servers respond quickly. Covers the request-response cycle, TCP three-way handshake, persistent connections, pipelining and why browsers disabled it, HTTP head-of-line blocking, chunked transfer encoding, caching and conditional requests, parallel connections and domain sharding, TCP slow start, the binary framing layer, and how streams/messages/frames enable multiplexing. Each concept includes a plain-language explanation, a real-world analogy, and practical debugging or tuning tips (curl, Wireshark, nginx keepalive settings, Lighthouse, WebPageTest). Positioned as part 1 of a series, ending on the promise that HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 address TCP's head-of-line blocking in part 2.

title: AI in Production Without a WHERE Clause
summary: A cartoon-framed opinion piece warns that AI assistants generating SQL statements remove the human pause that used to prevent destructive UPDATE or DELETE mistakes. The author (via a recurring cartoon character, Cardinal) proposes three cheap safeguards: give AI assistants read-only database access, wrap data-changing operations in explicit transactions with a row-count check before committing, and always write the WHERE clause before the verb. The piece argues AI can speed up writing queries, but a human should still hold the credentials that allow execution.

title: Introducing Motion UI Gallery
summary: Motion has launched a new premium React component called Gallery, part of Motion UI, for building image and video galleries with eight built-in 2D/3D arrangements (list, grid, barrel, coverflow, helix, ring, sphere, stack). Everything renders in the DOM using CSS transforms rather than canvas or WebGL, preserving accessibility, real img/video elements, and SEO. Key features include smooth transitions between arrangements regardless of current animation state, shared-element detail views with automatic high-res asset loading, drag/scroll/keyboard gestures, velocity-based modifiers like tilt and ripple, and custom arrangement definitions via defineGalleryArrangement. The base bundle is 19.6kb (25.8kb with detail view). Gallery is included in the Motion+ lifetime membership alongside other premium APIs, Motion UI examples, and a private Discord community.

title: JavaScript Microtasks vs Tasks: What Runs First?
summary: A step-by-step explainer of JavaScript's event loop scheduling, focused on the distinction between tasks (like setTimeout callbacks) and microtasks (like Promise.then and queueMicrotask callbacks). Uses a series of progressively complex code examples to show why synchronous code always runs first, why Promise callbacks run before setTimeout callbacks, how nested microtasks are processed within the same checkpoint, and how continuous microtask scheduling can cause 'microtask starvation' that blocks the event loop from reaching timer callbacks.

title: A deep dive into OpenSEO
summary: A deep architectural walkthrough of OpenSEO, an open-source SEO platform combining keyword research, competitor analysis, backlinks, site audits, and AI-visibility tracking. Built on TanStack Start, React, and Cloudflare bindings (D1, R2, KV, Workflows, Durable Objects), it pulls market data from DataForSEO and model access from OpenRouter. The piece traces how keyword research, rank tracking, the site audit crawler, MCP tool access, the in-app SAM agent, report generation, and Search Console/GA4 integrations are implemented, along with caching strategy, multi-tenant authorization, paid-request failure handling, and the trade-offs between the hosted service and self-hosting via Docker or Cloudflare with Alchemy.

title: EP229: 8 Chunking strategies for RAG-based agents
summary: A newsletter roundup covering eight chunking strategies for RAG-based agents: fixed-size, recursive, document-based, semantic, LLM-based, agentic, late chunking, and hierarchical, each briefly described with tradeoffs like cost versus quality. The issue also touches on neural machine translation internals behind Google Translate, how Agent Skills let LLM agents load reusable playbooks on demand to save context, and a short architectural comparison of PostgreSQL's process-based model versus MySQL's thread-based model.

title: plMail: A Self-Hosted Gmail Alternative
summary: plMail is a new free, open-source, AGPL-3.0 licensed webmail client that lets you self-host a unified inbox for existing IMAP, Gmail, and Outlook accounts without taking over mail delivery. It syncs messages into a PostgreSQL database on your own server, offering threaded conversations, unified inbox, search operators, filters, labels, and calendar sync with Google, Microsoft, and CalDAV. It ships with official Docker Compose support for AMD64/ARM64 and a TrueNAS app. Optional local AI features via Ollama can draft replies, summarize threads, or search by meaning, but are disabled by default. The project is young, with a maintainer who notes the iOS app needs more work, limited Proton Mail Bridge support, and solo maintenance, plus an important caveat that the database and the separate secrets file for credential encryption must both be backed up. The piece frames this as a response to Google retiring Gmailify and desktop POP-fetching by January 2027.

title: No more tech debt
summary: A software engineer recounts completing a design system migration that unified styles across React, HTMX, and Jinja stacks, replacing the unsupported JoyUI library with a custom Tailwind + ShadCN/BaseUI component system. The approach started with small tooling (a DESIGN.md guide, linters, minimal component library), followed by a big-bang migration PR, a month of iterative polish, then a second large push using AI coding agents. One agent session ran 6-7 hours and dropped @mui/joy imports from 592 files to 146 in a week, producing 45 pull requests across 8 stacks. The piece argues that thorough cleanup matters because AI agents amplify existing codebase patterns rather than reasoning from first principles, so leaving no trace of old code lets agents build consistently good UI going forward.

title: Show HN: Spotatui, a Spotify TUI/GUI without web API rate limits
summary: Spotatui is a community-maintained, actively developed Rust fork of spotify-tui that adds native Spotify streaming (no spotifyd or official app needed) plus several other music sources: local files, Subsonic/Navidrome, internet radio, YouTube, Qobuz, and Apple Music on macOS. It ships synced lyrics, a real-time audio visualizer, cross-source queueing, playlist sync, Lua plugins, listening history/recap, a full CLI, and a preview desktop app. An AI DJ feature exposes playback and history as MCP tools so coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) or a built-in TUI chat can pick music, using an existing agent subscription or local models instead of requiring an API key. Installation is available via a one-line script, Homebrew, Cargo, AUR, Winget, and Nix flakes across Linux, macOS, and Windows.
